data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 scopes its claim to 'low-complexity, high-criticality' omission-driven tasks, a restriction the problem never imposes, and then relies on the undefounded assertion that non-experts will 'treat every checklist item as a novel requirement, ensuring 100% coverage.' This conflates lack of familiarity with conscientious coverage; a non-expert fatigued by repetitive checklist use, or one who rubber-stamps items without performing the verification, would yield compliance without reliability. More importantly, SRC_002 gives no within-evaluation evidence that distinguishes genuine reliability from checklist compliance tracking the right answer. For omission-dominated tasks the requested discriminating evidence would be something like item-level process traces or attentional checks showing the non-expert actually performed each verification rather than endorsing by default — the target supplies none.
